findings.label: N3
findings.problem: StopsService.removeStops looks up each stop's day first, then removes the stops one at a time. When the list names the same stop twice, the first removal works. The second call to day.removeStops then throws "These stops aren't on the day". That message gives the wrong reason: the stop was on the day, and the real problem is that the list repeats it. The whole write is still rolled back, so no data is wrong.
findings.failure_case: I ran it on the Moab example. Calling services.stops.removeStops(itinerary, [s, s]) with the sunrise hike stop threw "These stops aren't on the day: a sunrise hike (stop_gq9wa5pz)." The coordinator is told a stop that exists isn't on its day.
findings.label_reason: The call is refused correctly. Only the error text is wrong, and an error with the wrong reason is N3, not F1 or F2. The code is new in this change, so the mark is nit.

findings.problem: refuseRejectedPlaces lists every rejected place in one sentence but always says "so it can't be a candidate". With two or more places, the text reads "The user rejected A, B, so it can't be a candidate", and it isn't clear which place "it" means.
findings.failure_case: Two rejected places, Kitschy motel and Red Sands Hotel, are offered in one lodging set. The error reads "The user rejected Kitschy motel, Red Sands Hotel, so it can't be a candidate. No candidates were added."
findings.label_reason: The text isn't false, since both places are named and the whole set is refused. It's only unclear, which is N3. The function is new in this change, so the mark is nit.
